reference_choice: substitute freely between two models based on a predicted per-prompt quality signal compared to a fixed threshold
question: When a request names a model, may the router serve a different one from a declared equivalent set, and on what evidence?
default: substitute within the declared equivalent set when the request permits it, using a per-request predicted quality signal
alternatives: always serve exactly the model named
substitute only when the named model is unavailable
substitute freely within the declared equivalent set on a per-request quality estimate
rationale: Every reference system that has a quality signal uses it to substitute; the shipped harness makes substitution legal and books quality from the served model.

reference_choice: no dollar bound at all; only an indirect bound on the share of traffic sent to the expensive option
question: Is spend bounded by anything other than the traffic itself?
default: a price-aware preference with no hard ceiling
alternatives: a price-aware preference with no hard ceiling
a hard spend ceiling per window that changes behaviour once crossed
rationale: Reference systems split: this one has only a soft preference, gateways ship hard budgets. Cost carries weight 3.0 in the scored objective, so this is consequential.

reference_choice: deterministic per-prompt decision for trained routers; an unbounded decision tally is the only growing state
question: Must two replays of the same trace produce the same decisions?
alternatives: decisions may differ between runs as long as the outcome distribution is the same
rationale: Every trained reference router is a pure function of the prompt, and a scored replay that cannot be reproduced cannot be audited.

reference_choice: the served model is visible; the reason is not
question: After the fact, must an operator be able to see why a given request went where it did?
default: the chosen target is recorded but the reason need not be
alternatives: the chosen target is recorded but the reason need not be
the chosen target and the deciding signal are both recorded per request
rationale: The harness scores from its own books, so self-reporting cannot move the score; recording the target is the common floor across the reference systems.
